svg.title: Halo bridge soldered stack
svg.desc: ESP32-S3 Super Mini stacked on an ESP32-C3 Super Mini, both face up, joined by four header pins: S3 GPIO1 to C3 GPIO7, C3 GPIO8 to S3 GPIO2, 5V and GND. (c) 2026 espboards.dev. Board illustrations: espboards.dev, licensed CC BY-NC 4.0: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-nc/4.0/
svg.text: S3 on top, C3 underneath, both face up and the same way round: USB ends together, antennas together.
dashed: the C3 underneath (1 mm shorter)

g.data-note: GPIO, ADC pin, SPI Master In Slave Out, PWM
GPIO, SPI Master Out Slave In, PWM

svg.text: Edge views: 4 header pins through both boards, all other pads left empty
Left edge: S3 TX, RX, 1-7 over C3 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 20, 21
Right edge: S3 5V, GND, 3V3, 13-8 over C3 5V, GND, 3V3, 4-0
The S3's back has 20 bare plated holes and the B+/B- battery pads. With the S3 on top they face the C3's parts:
leave enough gap to clear the C3's USB-C socket and buttons, and put insulating tape (Kapton) on the S3's back.
Solder only these four pins. The S3's pads marked TX and RX are GPIO43/44, not the pins used here.
With the S3 on top, the C3's BOOT and RESET buttons are covered; the C3 updates over Wi-Fi after its first USB flash.
